balance.what: the two data-movement terms merlin.perf.contract declares UNKNOWN, measured from a controlled transfer-size series on a cycle-accurate engine
balance.why_this_construction: perf/contract.py:449 names it -- 'Needs a measurement at >=2 transfer sizes to separate the rate from the fixed per-transfer cost'. A fit over the existing corpus is REFUTED: the same declared byte volume measured cycle counts disagreeing by 13.3x, because those are different emitted programs at one volume.

notes: exact rational least squares; the coefficients do not round on the way out

the fixed per-transfer cost is 128.5 cycles against a smallest measured transfer of 40 B, so the intercept dominates this domain and the slope is the MARGINAL rate over it -- not the bandwidth a large transfer achieves
balance.ridge_licence: the slope is a MARGINAL rate over the measured domain and, where the intercept dominates, a LOWER bound on what a large transfer can achieve -- so peak_compute divided by it is an UPPER bound on the ridge. An intensity above that bound is provably compute-bound; an intensity below it proves NOTHING and is not evidence of being memory-bound.

balance.structural_corroboration: the measured marginal rate is 16.119 bytes/cycle and one row of the 16x16 int8 mesh is 16 bytes. The proximity is CORROBORATION, not a derivation: the fit measures 16.119 and 16 is a plausible structural explanation for it, not its source.
